column7: Exposes the (authority, subject) pair that keys journey-status ownership, so a wrong pair would silently scope status to the wrong owner.
Builds the length-prefixed actor id that account_strategies compares to the prepared actor, so a collision would silently weaken that binding check.
Decides whether a principal counts as verified: the sole-operator assertion yields None, so proof-requiring consumers refuse it (authentication decision)

Private helper of check_issuer: its None is the IssuerUnreadable refusal and its scheme-host-port is the value check_issuer's equality refuses on when a recorded token endpoint contradicts the attested issuer

Non-unix occurrence of the unix mode/owner check on the legacy credential file; it allows unconditionally and the privacy refusal is the DACL test in read_legacy_source, held critical under the stricter-tier rule so the cfg-gated twin keeps the 95% obligation
Wires the durable once-only force-refresh claim that stops a 401 buying repeat provider calls; decision itself is in storage::commit.
Wires a grant write to the account key under the authority lock; the binding and refusal live in storage::commit but a mistake here bypasses them.
Wires the whole-version fence of a provider-rejected grant under one lock acquisition; decision itself is in storage::commit.
Debug impl that redacts access/refresh tokens; a mistake would silently leak credentials into logs.
Debug impl that redacts the secret key-reference names; a mistake would silently leak them.
Creates the custody store (locks, sealed authority) via storage::initialize; a mistake would silently stand up an unprotected or replaced store.
Resolves accounts config and key references, refuses absent or invalid config, and hands the resolved store to the initializer; a mistake would silently create a store with wrong keys or roots.
The single authority-mutex acquisition point every custody operation goes through; a mistake would silently break the atomic version fence and commit exclusion.
Validates the full five-field principal/backend/resource/issuer key before lookup and refuses a poisoned store, so one principal's record is resolved only by its exact digest.
Wires the descriptor-revision fence that forces re-consent; decision itself is in storage::commit.
Opens the existing authority via storage::open and treats absence as an error; a mistake would silently fall back to an unverified or fresh store.
Passes the expected grant version into storage::commit::refresh_tokens under the lock; a mistake would silently drop the compare-and-swap that rejects stale refreshes.
Builds the production provider transport and starts custody; a mistake would silently start without the validated provider.
Orders provider issuer-metadata bootstrap before opening the store and locks, so a rejected descriptor refuses startup; reordering would silently disable that check.
Recognises a refusal as account-marked from unsealed data, so a mistake would let non-resolver errors drive a connect offer for an account id.
Builds the AAD that binds the sealed authority to key id and instance; a mistake silently drops that binding.
Builds the authority with a fresh random store epoch that token AAD binds to; a constant epoch would disable replay separation.
Length-prefixed AAD encoding the token and authority ciphertext bindings rely on; an ambiguous encoding would silently weaken record binding.
Strict lowercase-hex length check that refuses malformed digests, generations and basenames read from disk records.
Decides whether a path prefix component is acceptable in a store path; unix returns false so any prefix is refused.
Mints the unguessable generation and record names the store relies on; a weak or constant value would silently undermine record identity.
Reads a candidate record under the measured size limit and maps every refusal to StorageUnavailable, never absence.
Computes the byte bound on reading a disk record so an untrusted file cannot force an unbounded read.
Returns a retained grant only for Connected or ReconnectRequired entries after digest and version authenticity checks, else None.
Decides whether a backend 401 triggers a single forced refresh and whether a reconnect-required state is surfaced as a refusal.
Pointer-identity check that a lease was minted by the currently installed strategy, so a replaced custody's credential is refused.
Binds descriptor, revision and the sole_operator assertion that later gate principal and fencing; a wrong value silently changes who is served.
Pairs the prepared credential with a ManagedLease holding this strategy, which the later recheck and minted_by comparison depend on.
Resolves the verified identity into an account-scoped credential for the backend via prepare, refusing when custody denies release.
Maps a custody refusal to the propagation error, deciding which states stay a closed Refuse versus typed connect states, never falling back.
Derives the per-account cache binding only if the account resolves and passes the descriptor-revision fence, scoping cache entries by owner.
Revokes freshly exchanged tokens at the provider on every refused-commit exit, so a mistake would silently leave live tokens for a grant that was refused.
Passes the journey owner key and expected fence to commit_journey_grant_if, so a wrong argument would silently disable the supersede fence or mis-scope the stored grant.
